checks.description: GET /api/tickets with no Authorization header at all
checks.evidence: HTTP 401, 0 tickets returned to an UNAUTHENTICATED request (no cookie, no bearer token, no API key of any kind beyond what a public browser tab has). The disposable canary ticket from this run was absent in the response. Per-row fields observed: raw_text=absent, customer_email=absent. Full response body is NOT persisted to disk or printed - this count and field-presence check is the only evidence kept, to avoid writing real customers' unredacted PII into a test report.

checks.description: GET /api/user_tickets?userId=<victim> with no proof of being that user (IDOR)
checks.evidence: HTTP 401, request supplied ONLY customer B's userId (a UUID with no other secret) and no Authorization header whatsoever, and the route returned 0 row(s) with HTTP 200 rather than 401/403. The route filters by the supplied userId but never verifies the caller IS that user.
